This occurred due to significant heat gains from the higher ambient conditions, which affected the TES and the PCM, even during the two-phase melting stages. While the modified model accounted for heat gains due to convection, the more extreme heat gain may be better captured if the current PCM DSC temperature- enthalpy linear curve fits are replaced with higher-order polynomials. Nonetheless, the overall system-level predictions were acceptable, with the maximum cooling capacity error less than 4%. The compressor discharge pressure was slightly underpredicted because check valves were installed in the experimental setup's discharge lines for mode switching, which may have caused a pressure build-up in the discharge line. Nonetheless, some experimental interruptions occurred during discharge due to a leak in the three-way valves, resulting in refrigerant charge escaping to the (low-pressure) outdoor loop. This prompted the operation to be manually switched to standard heating for a brief period to recapture any lost refrigerant. Model validations were conducted, employing the same HP-TES discharge model modifications as in the cooling mode (i.e., convective heat gains/losses in the TES, water thermal mass, and HTC verifications).
